questions.question: What are the two important characteristics that define survey research?

answers.text: Variables are measured using self-reports, and considerable attention is paid to sampling
Variables are manipulated experimentally, and data are collected in laboratory settings
Data are collected through observation, and small convenience samples are used
Participants are randomly assigned to conditions, and objective measures are used

answers.text: Participants primed to feel anger perceived less risk than those primed to feel fear
Participants primed to feel fear perceived less risk than those primed to feel anger
There was no difference in risk perception between anger and fear conditions
Both anger and fear priming increased risk perceptions equally

questions.question: What was the outcome of the 1936 presidential election polling that demonstrated the effectiveness of careful survey methodology?

answers.text: George Gallup correctly predicted Roosevelt's landslide victory using scientific methods with smaller samples

questions.question: According to the cognitive model of survey responding, what is the first step respondents engage in when answering a survey item?

answers.text: Interpreting the question
Retrieving relevant information from memory

questions.question: What is an item-order effect in survey research?

answers.text: When the order in which items are presented affects people's responses
When respondents always choose the first option presented
When items at the end of a survey are answered more accurately
When demographic items influence responses to substantive questions

answers.text: The correlation between the two increased from −.12 to +.66
The correlation between the two decreased from +.66 to −.12

answers.text: Brief, Relevant, Unambiguous, Specific, and Objective
Balanced, Reliable, Unbiased, Simple, and Organized
Basic, Reasonable, Understandable, Short, and Open-ended

questions.question: What is a 'double-barrelled' questionnaire item?

answers.text: An item that asks about two conceptually separate issues but allows only one response
An item that provides two correct answers among the response options
An item that is asked twice in different sections of the survey
An item that requires respondents to answer both yes and no

questions.question: According to the chapter, how many response options do five-point scales work best for?

answers.text: Unipolar scales where only one construct is tested
Bipolar scales where there is a dichotomous spectrum
All types of rating scales equally
Open-ended questions only

questions.question: What is a true Likert scale as originally developed by Rensis Likert?

answers.text: A scale involving agreement/disagreement with multiple statements, where responses are summed to produce an attitude score
Any rating scale ranging from 1 to 5 or 1 to 7
A scale measuring only positive attitudes toward a topic
A visual-analog scale with endpoints labeled

questions.question: What should generally be true of response categories for categorical variables in closed-ended items?

answers.text: They should be mutually exclusive and exhaustive
They should overlap to capture all possible nuances
They should include only the most common responses
They should be limited to exactly three options

What is simple random sampling?

answers.text: A method where each individual in the population has an equal probability of being selected
A method where researchers select the most convenient participants
A method where the population is divided into strata before sampling
A method where participants volunteer to be in the study

questions.question: What is stratified random sampling?

answers.text: The population is divided into subgroups and a random sample is taken from each subgroup
All members of specific subgroups are automatically included in the sample
Participants are selected based on their proximity to the researcher
The sample is stratified after data collection is complete

questions.question: What is the key advantage of cluster sampling?

answers.text: It does not require a sampling frame and minimizes travel for face-to-face interviews
It guarantees that all subgroups are proportionally represented
It is the most statistically precise form of probability sampling
It eliminates all forms of sampling bias

questions.question: Why was the Literary Digest's 1936 presidential poll inaccurate?

questions.question: What is non-response bias?

answers.text: Bias that occurs when survey non-responders differ from responders in systematic ways
Bias that occurs when respondents give socially desirable answers
Bias that occurs when the sampling frame is incomplete
Bias that occurs when questions are worded poorly

There was no difference between responders and non-responders
